prompt:
A table lists six physical quantities:
1. Mass
2. Velocity
3. Work
4. Acceleration
5. Power
6. Weight

(a) Identify the three scalar quantities from the list. [1]
(b) Identify the three vector quantities from the list. [1]
(c) State the fundamental property that distinguishes the vector quantities from the scalar quantities. [1]

answer.text:
(a) Scalars: Mass, Work, Power.
(b) Vectors: Velocity, Acceleration, Weight.
(c) Direction (vectors have direction as well as magnitude, whereas scalars have magnitude only).

mark_scheme: Part (a) [1 mark]: Mass, Work, Power (all 3 required for 1 mark).
Part (b) [1 mark]: Velocity, Acceleration, Weight (all 3 required for 1 mark).
Part (c) [1 mark]: Direction (vectors have direction / scalars do not have direction).
hints: Work and power are forms/rates of energy transfer, which are scalars.
Weight is the gravitational force on an object, which acts downward (a vector).
solution:
(a) Scalars: Mass, Work, Power.
(b) Vectors: Velocity, Acceleration, Weight.
(c) Direction is the property possessed by vectors in addition to magnitude.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Check scalars: mass (kg), work (J), power (W) have no direction (1 mark).
Step 2: Check vectors: velocity (m s^-1), acceleration (m s^-2), weight (N downward) have direction (1 mark).
Step 3: State distinguishing property: direction (1 mark).
